title: 广交会生存指南：第一次参展如何把流量变订单
titleEn: Canton Fair Survival Guide: Turn Booth Traffic into Orders on Your First Show
description: Emma和James聊广交会参展那些事，从展前精准邀约、展位布置技巧、现场15分钟高效沟通法，到展后72小时黄金跟进，用轻松对话帮你第一次参展就能从容应对，把流量变成订单。

lines.speaker: emma
lines.en: Welcome back to TradeTalk, everyone. I am Emma, and with me as always is James. Today we are talking about something very timely: the Canton Fair is coming up in October, and many new exporters are wondering how to make the most of it.
lines.cn: 欢迎回到TradeTalk，我是Emma，和往常一样James也在。今天我们聊一个非常应景的话题：10月份广交会就要来了，很多外贸新人都在想怎么才能充分利用好这次展会。

lines.speaker: james
lines.en: That is right, James here. I remember my first Canton Fair. I just stood there smiling, handing out catalogs, and by the end I had a pile of business cards but zero orders. It took me a few shows to figure out that a trade show is a system, not just a booth.
lines.cn: 没错，我是James。我还记得第一次参加广交会，我就站在那里微笑，发目录，结束时我有一堆名片但零订单。我花了几次展会才明白，展会是一套系统，不只是摆个摊位。

lines.speaker: emma
lines.en: Exactly. So let us break it down into three stages: before the show, during the show, and after the show. James, what is the most important thing to do before the show?
lines.cn: 正是。那我们分三个阶段来讲：展前、展中和展后。James，展前最重要的事情是什么？

lines.speaker: james
lines.en: Most people think the show starts when you arrive in Guangzhou. But actually, it starts one month before. You need to identify your target customers and reach out to them on LinkedIn or by email. Tell them you will be at the fair, invite them to your booth, and even book specific meeting times. The best customers are the ones you schedule before the show, not the random walk-ins.
lines.cn: 很多人以为展会是从你到广州才开始的。但实际上，一个月前就开始了。你需要识别目标客户，通过LinkedIn或邮件联系他们。告诉他们你会参加展会，邀请他们到你的展位，甚至预约具体的面谈时间。最好的客户是你展前就约好的，而不是随机走进来的。

lines.speaker: emma
lines.en: That is such a good point. A lot of new exporters just show up and hope for the best. But if you have 20 pre-scheduled meetings, you already know the show will be productive. Now, what about the booth itself? How should you set it up?
lines.cn: 这点太重要了。很多新人只是到场然后碰运气。但如果你有20个预先约好的会面，你就已经知道展会会有收获了。那展位本身呢？应该怎么布置？

lines.speaker: james
lines.en: The number one rule: your booth should tell people what you do in three seconds. If someone walks by and cannot tell you sell markers and highlighters, you have failed. Put your best-selling products at eye level, use good lighting, and have a clear background board. Also, do not clutter the booth with too many products. Focus on three to five hero products that tell your story.
lines.cn: 首要原则：你的展位应该在3秒内告诉别人你是做什么的。如果有人走过却看不出你卖马克笔和荧光笔，你就失败了。把最畅销的产品放在视线高度，用好灯光，有清晰的背景板。另外，不要在展位上堆太多产品，专注于3到5个能讲述你品牌故事的主打产品。

lines.speaker: emma
lines.en: And do not forget the small things: business cards, a tablet to show product videos, printed catalogs, test reports for EN71 and ASTM, and some small customized gifts. People love free things, and a useful gift with your logo keeps your brand in their mind.
lines.cn: 还有不要忘记小物件：名片、展示产品视频的平板、印刷目录、EN71和ASTM的检测报告，以及一些定制小礼品。人们喜欢免费的东西，一个印有你logo的实用小礼品能让你的品牌留在他们脑海里。

lines.speaker: james
lines.en: Now, the most important part: what do you do when a customer walks into your booth? The biggest mistake new people make is they immediately start selling. They say, welcome, what do you want, how much do you need? That is overwhelming.
lines.cn: 现在是最重要的部分：客户走进展位时你该怎么做？新人最大的错误就是立刻开始推销。他们说，欢迎，你要什么，要多少。这让人有压力。

lines.speaker: emma
lines.en: Right. You should start with a warm welcome and an open question. Something like, welcome to our booth, are you looking for markers or highlighters specifically? Then you listen. Let the customer tell you what they need. You should be doing 30 percent of the talking and 70 percent of the listening in the first five minutes.
lines.cn: 对。你应该先热情欢迎，然后问一个开放式问题。比如，欢迎来到我们展位，您具体是在找马克笔还是荧光笔？然后你倾听。让客户告诉你他们需要什么。前五分钟你应该说30%，听70%。

lines.speaker: james
lines.en: And here is a pro tip: take notes on the back of their business card. Write down what they are interested in, their target price, quantity, and any special requirements. When you get back to the hotel at night, you will thank yourself. Most people end up with a pile of identical business cards and no memory of who wanted what.
lines.cn: 还有一个专业技巧：在他们的名片背面记笔记。写下他们对什么感兴趣、目标价格、数量和任何特殊要求。晚上回到酒店时，你会感谢自己的。大多数人最后是一堆一模一样的名片，完全不记得谁要了什么。

lines.speaker: emma
lines.en: That is such good advice. Now, what about the 15-minute rule? You mentioned that earlier.
lines.cn: 这个建议太好了。那15分钟规则呢？你之前提到过。

lines.speaker: james
lines.en: Yes, the 15-minute rule. At a busy show, you cannot spend an hour with each customer. You need to be efficient. In 15 minutes, you should accomplish four things: first, understand their needs and target market. Second, show them the relevant products and key selling points. Third, give them the key business terms: MOQ, lead time, price range. Fourth, get their contact info and agree on the next step. If you can do those four things in 15 minutes, you have had a successful meeting.
lines.cn: 对，15分钟规则。在繁忙的展会上，你不能每个客户花一小时。你需要高效。在15分钟内，你应该完成四件事：第一，了解他们的需求和目标市场。第二，展示相关产品和核心卖点。第三，给出关键商务条款：MOQ、交货期、价格范围。第四，拿到他们的联系方式并约定下一步。如果你能在15分钟内完成这四件事，这次会面就是成功的。

lines.speaker: emma
lines.en: And when the customer is ready to leave, do not just say thank you and bye. You need to recap what you discussed and commit to a specific follow-up action. For example, it was great meeting you, as discussed you are interested in our refillable highlighters for the German market, I will send you a detailed quotation and sample offer by tomorrow morning. Then add their WhatsApp right there.
lines.cn: 客户准备离开时，不要只说谢谢再见。你需要回顾讨论内容，并承诺具体的跟进行动。比如，很高兴认识您，正如讨论的您对我们面向德国市场的可换芯荧光笔感兴趣，我会在明天上午之前给您发送详细报价单和样品方案。然后当场加他们的WhatsApp。

lines.speaker: james
lines.en: That brings us to the after-show part, which is where most people fail. They come back from the show, exhausted, and they let the leads go cold. The golden window is 72 hours. Within 72 hours, you need to send a personalized follow-up email to every serious lead.
lines.cn: 这就到了展后部分，这是大多数人失败的地方。他们从展会回来，筋疲力尽，然后让线索变冷。黄金窗口是72小时。在72小时内，你需要给每个重要线索发送个性化的跟进邮件。

lines.speaker: emma
lines.en: And not a generic email. You need to reference your specific conversation. Mention the products they were interested in, the quantity they mentioned, and attach a photo of you two together at the booth if you took one. People receive dozens of follow-up emails after a show, the personalized ones get opened, the generic ones get deleted.
lines.cn: 而且不是通用邮件。你需要提到你们具体的对话。提到他们感兴趣的产品、提到的数量，如果拍了合影就附上你们在展位的合照。展会后人们会收到几十封跟进邮件，个性化的会被打开，通用的会被删除。

lines.speaker: james
lines.en: Also, categorize your leads into A, B, and C tiers. A tier customers have clear demand and budget, follow up within 24 hours with a detailed quotation and sample offer. B tier customers are interested but not ready yet, send a thank you email and keep in touch with new product updates. C tier are just browsing, add them to your newsletter list. Do not waste the same amount of energy on every lead.
lines.cn: 还有，把你的线索分成A、B、C三类。A类客户有明确需求和预算，24小时内跟进，发送详细报价单和样品方案。B类客户感兴趣但还没准备好，发送感谢邮件并通过新品更新保持联系。C类只是随便看看，把他们加入你的邮件通讯列表。不要在每个线索上浪费同样多的精力。

lines.speaker: emma
lines.en: That is a great framework. Before we wrap up, any final advice for first-time exhibitors?
lines.cn: 这个框架太棒了。结束前，对第一次参展的人有什么最终建议吗？

lines.speaker: james
lines.en: Yes, three things. First, wear comfortable shoes, you will be standing for 10 hours a day. Second, stay hydrated and keep snacks at the booth, you may not have time for lunch. Third, and most importantly, remember that the show is just the beginning. The real work happens in the follow-up. A show with 100 leads and zero follow-up is worse than a show with 10 leads and perfect follow-up.
lines.cn: 有，三件事。第一，穿舒服的鞋，你每天要站10小时。第二，保持水分，在展位上放些零食，你可能没时间吃午饭。第三，也是最重要的，记住展会只是开始。真正的工作在跟进中。100个线索但零跟进的展会，不如10个线索但完美跟进的展会。

lines.speaker: emma
lines.en: Perfect advice. That is all for today. Thank you for listening to TradeTalk. Good luck at the Canton Fair, and we will see you next time.
lines.cn: 完美的建议。今天就到这里。感谢收听TradeTalk。祝你们广交会好运，我们下次见。
